claims.text: Pramipexole: patients have fallen asleep during daily activities, including driving;
claims.quote: Patients treated with pramipexole have reported falling asleep while engaged in activities of daily living, including the operation of motor vehicles which sometimes resulted in accidents.
claims.locator: 5.1 Falling Asleep During Activities of Daily Living and Somnolence

claims.quote: Sudden onset of sleep may occur without warning

claims.text: Before starting, advise about drowsiness and ask about sedating drugs or alcohol and sleep disorders.
claims.quote: advise patients of the potential to develop drowsiness and specifically ask about factors that may increase the risk for somnolence with pramipexole dihydrochloride tablets such as the use of concomitant sedating medications or alcohol, the presence of sleep disorders
claims.locator: 5.1 Falling Asleep During Activities of Daily Living and Somnolence

claims.text: Dopamine antagonists (eg, neuroleptics, metoclopramide) may reduce ropinirole's efficacy
claims.quote: • Dopamine antagonists (e.g., neuroleptics, metoclopramide): May reduce efficacy of ropinirole tablets

Since pramipexole is a dopamine agonist, it is possible that dopamine antagonists, such as the neuroleptics (phenothiazines, butyrophenones, thioxanthenes) or metoclopramide, may diminish the effectiveness of pramipexole

claims.text: Ropinirole is metabolized by CYP1A2: ciprofloxacin raises its levels and smoking is expected to increase its clearance; adjust the dose when a potent CYP1A2 inducer or inhibitor is started or stopped.
claims.quote: Therefore, if therapy with a drug known to be a potent inducer or inhibitor of CYP1A2 is stopped or started during treatment with ropinirole tablets, adjustment of the dose of ropinirole tablets may be required. Coadministration of ciprofloxacin, an inhibitor of CYP1A2, increases the AUC and C max of ropinirole [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)]. Cigarette smoking is expected to increase the clearance of ropinirole since CYP1A2 is known to be induced by smoking
